We need to implement the task. The previous attempt had a patch command that was malformed. Need to create repository with proper files: server.js, maybe a simple HTML in public folder, and client JS.

We must use Node.js built-in http and sqlite. No external deps.

Implement SQLite DB with table projects (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name TEXT NOT NULL). Use DB_PATH env var.

Server must serve static files from public folder, handle API endpoints:

- GET /health -> JSON

- GET /api/projects -> list projects

- POST /api/projects -> create project; body JSON {name}. Trim, if empty return 400 with error message.

- GET /api/projects/:id -> get single project.

Potentially also serve project page.

But front-end can just navigate to /projects/<id> which is served by static file (maybe same index.html with routing client-side). Simpler: server serves same index.html for any path (except API and /health). Use fallback.

When button clicked, send POST to /api/projects, then refresh list.

When list shows rows with data-testid="project-row" and button Open project linking to /projects/<id>.

On /projects/<id> page, display heading with project name and button back.

We can implement a simple SPA using vanilla JS with hash or path detection. Since we serve same HTML, client script reads location.pathname, decides view.

Implement alert for validation error: show visible alert element.

No external deps; we must use node:sqlite (experimental). Actually Node 22 includes built-in sqlite module? Node has "node:sqlite" experimental API. We'll use that.

Write server.js using import syntax (ES modules). Use http, fs, path, url, sqlite.

Implement async initialization of DB.

Serve static files: read files from public folder.

For any request not starting with /api or /health, serve index.html.

Implement API endpoints.

Now we need to commit changes. Use git commands.
